context.continuation_reason: AWS unexpectedly accepted unweighted $LATEST aliases; the first weighted call correctly rejected this primary and ended that capture. Its native observations and full cleanup are retained; routing continues on a fresh owned function.
context.signing_correction: The initial transport signed percent-encoded paths without the additional canonical URI encoding required by SigV4. Its InvalidSignatureException observations are transport failures, not alias semantics. Correctly signed reserved-name and full-ARN calls follow in metadata capture.
context.payload_encoding: Invoke input.Payload is the base64-encoded SDK blob; wire_request.body is decoded JSON. result.output is decoded native response JSON; result.payload_base64 preserves native response bytes with account ID normalized before encoding. Code.Location is omitted entirely.

observed_findings.claim: Unweighted aliases accepted $LATEST as primary; attaching an additional version to that primary was rejected. The latest alias was also synchronously invoked with executed version $LATEST.
Successful empty and same-value UpdateAlias calls changed RevisionId. A stale RevisionId rejected the update without changing alias state.
Omitting RoutingConfig retained weights; an empty RoutingConfig object cleared them to native null. An empty AdditionalVersionWeights map also cleared them.
Changing primary while retaining a distinct secondary preserved weights; choosing the existing secondary as primary without clearing weights was rejected atomically.

Negative/over-one weights and $LATEST secondary keys yielded ValidationException. Primary-as-secondary, multiple secondary versions, mismatched execution roles and mismatched DLQ targets yielded InvalidParameterValueException. Missing secondary versions yielded ResourceNotFoundException. Observed failed live-alias mutations left state unchanged.
Exact 0 and 1 additional weights were accepted and retained. The bounded 0 sample executed primary and 1 sample secondary. The mixed sample is descriptive only, not an exact distribution guarantee.
Invoke executed-version headers matched context.function_version; direct version invocation context ARN used the numeric qualifier, while alias invocations retained the alias qualifier.
DeleteAlias was idempotent for an absent valid alias name on an existing function; recreation produced a new alias revision.

GetFunction and GetFunctionConfiguration for an alias, supplied either as Qualifier or full alias ARN, returned FunctionArn ending in the alias name while Version and configuration projected the primary published version.

ListAliases FunctionVersion filtering matched the primary version, not weighted secondary membership. A nonexistent numeric version returned an empty list. The observed unfiltered pages used alias-name NextMarker values; the arbitrary marker was accepted and returned a page. Native result order is retained without asserting a universal ordering rule.
